analysis.summary: A high-severity React Hook violation was found in the OrderOverview component that will cause a runtime crash.

bugs.title: React Hook Rule Violation (Conditional Hook Call)
bugs.description: The 'useTranslations' hook is called after several conditional early return statements (lines 408 and 415).
bugs.risk: React requires hooks to be called in the exact same order on every render. If 'loading' or 'orderError.showErrorPage' is true, this hook is skipped. When the state changes and the hook is subsequently called, React will throw a fatal runtime error ('Rendered more hooks than during the previous render'), crashing the application.

notBugs.reason: The different import paths for useTranslations in the iframe component vs the overview component likely reflect the project's architectural transition from legacy hooks to shared utility libraries; both usage patterns are internally consistent within their respective files.
While pcpPaymentResponse.code is optional in the interface, the equality check (code !== '200') is safe in JavaScript/TypeScript and will not cause a runtime crash if the property is undefined.

The functional state update in the iframe component correctly checks for the existence of prevData.cartModel before attempting to spread it, preventing potential null pointer exceptions during the async callback.
